retryInstructions.fullSentenceLinksNeedLeadIn: If a link stands alone as its own sentence or paragraph, or if a sentence mainly directs the user to a link, place that link direction in its own paragraph. Prefer putting a standalone link sentence or paragraph last in the alert content, but do not treat placement as a hard requirement. Use a natural lead-in before the anchor when the standalone link text does not already contain a clear action verb. "Refer to:" and "For details:" are both valid for supporting detail, reference, status, or explanatory links. Prefer "Refer to:" for required task, service, form, or procedural reference links. Prefer "For details:" when the link provides supporting information or more context. Prefer "Learn more:" for optional background, status, or update links. Do not add a lead-in before standalone action links such as "View CRA processing times", "Check CRA processing times", "Get an access code", "Sign up for direct deposit", "Create an account", "Cancel a payment", "Send documents", "Confirm your information", "Review the proposed rates", "Register a business", "Sign in or register for a CRA account", "Learn about the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit", "Find out how to get an access code", or "How to get an access code". Use "Learn about" without a colon when the linked text naturally completes the phrase, especially for explainer or topic pages. If the phrase needs an article, place it before the anchor, for example "Learn about the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit". Do not put a period or other punctuation after the closing anchor in a standalone link sentence or paragraph.
